C-RENDER-REVIEW-FIXES.IntentSummary: Fix the four renderer-surface defects of the approved C-RENDER-REVIEW-FIXES spec (findings 11-14 of the 2026-11-02 smart review) plus its recorded localization debts in one wave: honest async outcomes for every notification action (the card awaits handler/payload, a failing Reveal raises a localized warning notice, zero unhandled rejections — both editor.js reveal payloads at 2241 and 2371 return their promise), a rollback confirmation that cannot fail silently (the dynamic import moves inside the try, the component awaits the store action, any failure raises a localized error notice with the raw Rust detail kept to the console), a truthful copy pulse (copySelectionText reports the real clipboard outcome; the green pulse fires only after a successful write; failures stay silent per the accepted M-067 quiet-developer voice), and a fully localized rollback-feedback surface (rollback.restoreFailedTitle/Body replace the hardcoded English title and the raw Rust error string) including the visible GUI notice when a completed rollback skipped restoring preferences — fed by a new structured Rust fact: the restore path writes a minimal restore-outcome.json marker in the rollback data root at the shared logged-and-skipped site (stale copies removed at restore start), and a new read-and-clear command mt_rollback_restore_outcome lets the restored session's RUN_LAUNCH_CHECK show rollback.prefsSkippedTitle/Body exactly once. The Rust rollback core changes ONLY by that additive fact channel — no restore-logic reorder; the CLI stderr human lines stay English (a recorded decision: the CLI is a developer surface, every GUI-visible string goes through the ten-locale store). Execution discipline: single-writer serial arcs where files are shared — notificationCard/index.vue (T-003 then T-005) and store/autoUpdates.js (T-004 then T-006) as direct DAG arcs, with m068_rollback.rs serialized transitively (T-001 ≺ T-006 ≺ T-007); every other shared file is serialized by T-007's direct dependencies on T-003/T-004/T-005/T-006. Sequencing: the graph and verification deltas (T-007) share .grace/graph/features.xml and .grace/verification/features.xml with the in-flight C-STATS-READOUT T-007 — this change executes on a dedicated branch off fork/main and lands strictly after C-STATS-READOUT's graph deltas (rebase before T-007; the parallel-preflict overlap on those two files is the plan's conscious serial-ordering design, recorded here). Execution mode mirrors the archived C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES wave: branch fix/render-review-fixes off fork/main, PR under the strict ruleset with the squash retry cycle, governance label release:user-facing with close/reopen, train admission as a separate chore(train) commit per train rule 3. The plan's own review gate (four corners, two consecutive clean passes over spec and plan together) runs on this draft before approval is requested. Round-1 sharpening recorded: registering the command is the four-site chain (m001_validate.rs REGISTERED_COMMANDS, main.rs generate_handler!, src/renderer/src/ipc/contract/types.ts CommandMap + channel union, and the test/fixtures/ipc-channels/tauri.v2.json fixture regenerated via tools/gen-tauri-v2-fixture.mjs — the boot parity gate exits 1 on drift in either direction); the marker lives at rollback_root() itself, never inside the live/ set the restore consumes; the editor banner's copy pulse joins T-005 (the spec's Goal 3 is surface-general); the restore-failure notice carries severity error (the spec's literal "error notification") while the prefs-skip notice is a sticky warning (the sibling boot-surface pattern); and notifications.source.rollback becomes the seventh locale key (the rollback card's source chip today renders a raw key). T-001.Title: Rust structured restore-outcome fact and the read-and-clear command

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The GUI-shared restore path writes a minimal structured marker restore-outcome.json at the rollback root itself — rollback_root()/restore-outcome.json (inside gui_restore_verified derived from the live-set base via base.parent(), the established live/-sibling derivation, so the root-override test seam drives a temp root and never the real data root) — NEVER inside the live/ set the restore consumes (the skip site sits beside remove_dir_all(base) at m068_rollback.rs:1182, and boot finalization removes live/ again at :810; the root already hosts loose files — instance.lock, delegate.request, delegate.ack — so a root-level marker is layout-consistent and survives both removals) — written exactly at the existing logged-and-skipped preferences site (the macOS-only gui_restore_verified — the sole logged-and-skipped site; the Windows restore hard-aborts on a prefs failure and surfaces through the localized restore-failure notice instead), with content bounded to {"prefs":"skipped","error":"<free-form diagnostics truncated to 200 chars on char boundaries — multi-byte-safe; a byte-slice would panic on localized OS error text>","at":"<unix-seconds write time>"} — no dedicated path/digest/secret fields (a genuine io error may name a file in its Display text; the cap is the bound), asserted by test so the schema survives error-chain changes; the marker write itself is best-effort and non-fatal — a failed write logs a stderr marker and never alters the restore outcome or its exit code (the fact channel must not become a false-failure channel); every restore entry (gui_restore_core and restore_inner — the CLI and Windows-dialog entry) removes any stale marker first, and the prepare entry (update-install snapshot creation) clears an unconsumed marker by calling the same root-explicit removal helper — the helper takes the root explicitly and is tested directly on a TempDir (prepare_inner itself has no root seam and keeps its signature, per the file's own recorded test practice), its call site pinned by the removal-helper call appearing inside prepare_inner's own body — the fact's audience is the restored session's boots before the next update begins — and the at timestamp bounds the fact absolutely: the renderer suppresses anything older than 48 h with a console marker only, which is what closes the transition era (a restored pre-feature binary's own prepare cannot know the marker; the next new binary's first boot age-checks it instead of inheriting a weeks-old skip); a restore whose preferences succeed writes nothing (the CLI stderr human line and every restore step are otherwise byte-unchanged — the diff shows an additive fact channel only).

A new command mt_rollback_restore_outcome returns the parsed marker (or null when absent) and removes the file in the same call — one read-and-clear, idempotent on absent files; registration completes the four-site chain (the boot parity gate enforces the fixture↔allowlist pair in both directions — drift exits 1 at boot; the generate_handler! site is hand-synced per the m001 MODULE_CONTRACT, the ipc-contract site is covered transitively — the fixture is generated from the CommandMap by the gen tool — and both are enforced here by the TargetAssertions pins and the C-5 inspection): the name joins REGISTERED_COMMANDS beside mt_rollback_restore/mt_rollback_status, joins the generate_handler! list in main.rs (the M-068 cluster), joins src/renderer/src/ipc/contract/types.ts (CommandMap and the command-name union), and the fixture test/fixtures/ipc-channels/tauri.v2.json gains mt::rollback::restore_outcome beside its siblings — regenerated via node tools/gen-tauri-v2-fixture.mjs; the command also gains the app-store stub variant (the hand-written stub pattern of the m068 cluster), keeping cargo build --features app-store compilable — the stub returns Ok(null) (the status-stub pattern), so an app-store build's boot stays quiet instead of logging the fallback error; the read side enforces the same bounds as the write — an unparsable marker, or one whose error field exceeds the 200-char write-side cap, is treated as null and cleared; a schema-valid marker missing the at field is unparsable by the same strict-schema rule; header conventions honored — m001_validate.rs gains its CHANGE_SUMMARY line per the C-UPDATER-ROLLBACK precedent.

Rust unit tests (the existing #[cfg(test)] seams of m068_rollback.rs, in the style of prefs_skipped_line_is_human_and_truthful) prove: the skip path writes the marker with the truncated error string (the cap asserted with a long injected reason); the success path leaves no marker; a stale marker is removed when a new restore starts (both restore entries); the removal helper clears an unconsumed marker on a TempDir root (the prepare call site textually pinned — prepare_inner itself is not refactored); a failed marker write leaves the restore outcome unchanged (the best-effort pin); the written marker carries the at timestamp; an unparsable marker, one missing the at field, and one with an over-200-char error field read as null and clear — the cap test using a long multi-byte non-ASCII reason so truncation is proven char-boundary-safe; the marker SURVIVES the live-consuming step of a full gui_restore_verified run (the round-1 finding that motivated the root-level pin); the read-and-clear returns the record once and null thereafter.

T-002.Title: The seven feedback keys across all ten locales, gated

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The existing rollback locale family gains restoreFailedTitle and restoreFailedBody (honest rollback-failure copy: the previous version could not be restored, details in the log — never a promise to retry) and prefsSkippedTitle and prefsSkippedBody (the rollback itself completed, the saved settings could not be brought back, some settings may be back at their defaults); the existing notifications family gains actionFailedTitle and actionFailedBody (a quiet generic action-failure copy, not reveal-specific) and the source chip key notifications.source.rollback (the rollback card injects source: 'rollback' and every locale table lacks the key today, so the chip renders raw key text uppercased) — seven keys in all, each landing with non-empty native copy in all ten shipped locales (static/locales/*.json).

tests/renderer/i18n/locale-keys.test.js gains the rollback-feedback pin: the seven keys present and non-empty in all ten locale tables, in the C-TITLEBAR-MODE-CHIPS R-4 pattern; the existing modeChips and inventory guards stay untouched and green.

T-003.Title: Honest notification actions: the card awaits, a failing Reveal speaks

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: runAction becomes async (const runAction = async (action) => {) and awaits both action.handler() and action.payload(); a rejection is caught — console.error marker plus a warning notice titled/formed from notifications.actionFailedTitle/Body, its source carried from the failing action's own card (props.entry.source — honest provenance, not the SYSTEM default) — so no action rejection escapes as unhandled; the success paths are behavior-identical (same handlers, same dismissal semantics).
Both editor.js reveal payloads (2241 and 2371) return window.electron.shell.showItemInFolder(filePath) instead of discarding it, so the awaited card path observes the Tauri opener promise.

Renderer tests prove: an injected showItemInFolder rejection (per call site) surfaces the localized warning notice — its message equal to the localized notifications.actionFailedBody and containing none of the injected raw error string, its source the action's own card source — and produces zero unhandled promise rejections (vitest unhandledrejection capture); a resolving payload shows no notice; the handler branch still runs plain sync handlers.

T-004.Title: Rollback confirmation that cannot fail silently

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The dynamic @tauri-apps/api/core import moves inside the try of CONFIRM_ROLLBACK (the import rejection joins the invoke failure path); the catch keeps console.error with the raw error for logs and raises an error-severity notice (the spec's literal "error notification"; the store's own severity rule makes error notices sticky — a confirmed-but-failed rollback must not vanish; source: 'rollback', so the chip reads the new localized source key) titled/formed from rollback.restoreFailedTitle/Body — the raw Rust error string no longer reaches the GUI (title: 'Rollback failed' and message: String(e) are gone from the notice).

The rollbackConfirm component awaits store.CONFIRM_ROLLBACK() (await store.CONFIRM_ROLLBACK()) with its own catch reduced to a console marker — the store owns user feedback, the component owns rejection hygiene; the card-hiding order is unchanged (visible = false before the restore attempt remains the accepted UX: failure raises the notice instead of resurrecting the card).

Renderer tests prove: an injected dynamic-import failure raises the localized notice and leaves zero unhandled rejections (the finding-12 hole); an injected invoke rejection raises the same localized notice (title from the key, not the hardcoded English; severity error pinned by the test; the message equals the localized rollback.restoreFailedBody and contains none of the injected raw error string — the last line of defense for finding 14); the happy path restores exactly as today.

T-005.Title: Truthful copy: the pulse only follows a real clipboard write

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: copySelectionText reports the real outcome as a promise on EVERY path — Promise.resolve(false) for empty input and for a missing Clipboard API, writeText(text).then(() => true, () => false) for the write — so callers can chain unconditionally (chaining .then on a plain boolean false throws, and the vitest jsdom environment ships no navigator.clipboard, making the missing-API path the default test reality); the silent-failure contract of the M-067 quiet-developer voice stays (no toast, no notice), but the function never claims success it did not observe — including the synchronous-throw corner of writeText inside the try, whose catch path resolves false like every other failure (the whole body is wrapped: every path, thrown or not, returns a promise); the module-contract comments (corner C-4 block) are updated to say exactly that.

Both copy-on-select surfaces — the notificationCard and the editor banner (components/editorWithTabs/notifications.vue, the same copy-then-pulse shape the spec's surface-general Goal 3 covers) — pulse only on a resolved successful write, with the Range/Element captured synchronously in the release handler BEFORE the chain (inside the existing try, guarded by sel.rangeCount > 0 — a deferred getRangeAt can throw IndexSizeError past the handler's catch or pulse the wrong node after the selection collapses) and passed into the callback: copySelectionText(sel.toString()).then((ok) => { if (ok) applyCopyPulse(range) }).catch(() => {}) — a missing Clipboard API and a rejected writeText both produce no pulse; a successful write pulses exactly once; the reduced-motion and multi-node-range degradations are unchanged; the notificationsHistory caller keeps ignoring the return value (no behavior change there).

Renderer tests prove all three clipboard cases (absent API / rejected write / success) for the resolved value and for the pulse on BOTH surfaces (card and banner), plus the selection-collapsed-before-resolution case (no throw, no unhandled rejection — a captured Range is a frozen snapshot that survives the collapse, so on a successful write the pulse still lands on the captured node, which is honest feedback for a copy that did happen, and on an absent or rejected write there is no pulse) and the unchanged history-copy behavior; the card's copy-kind action call site (index.vue:164) keeps discarding the return value — unchanged, no pulse; the existing boolean pins in tests/renderer/services/notification-deep.test.js migrate to the promise contract (awaited, toBe on resolved values for the success/empty/rejecting/missing-API cases) with its applyCopyPulse and reduced-motion coverage untouched.

T-006.Title: The prefs-skip boot notice in the restored session

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The mt_rollback_restore_outcome query runs at the very start of RUN_LAUNCH_CHECK — BEFORE the updater gate's early return (autoUpdates.js:184-187) and every check path, on its own injectable option (outcomeInvokeFn) with the dynamic-import fallback — the shared invokeFn option stays exclusive to mt_updater_check, so the five existing invoke-count pins of autoUpdates.test.js (lines 249, 270, 356, 370, 385) stand untouched (the outcome query rides its own seam, so the injected invokeFn mock is never called by it — the dynamic-import fallback rejects quietly under jsdom), and the new tests inject outcomeInvokeFn directly — because the gate skips exactly the boots the notice targets (throttled <24 h after the install-time check stamp, whats-new-deferred, auto-check off); when the structured fact is present it raises a sticky warning notice (sticky: true, the sibling boot-surface pattern — an unpinned warning auto-dismisses in 10 s and the read-and-clear fact can never resurface; dedupKey: 'rollback-prefs-skipped' — the rollbackConfirm singleton pattern, so a future multi-window boot cannot stack the notice; source: 'rollback', so the chip reads the new localized source key) titled/formed from rollback.prefsSkippedTitle/Body; the notice copy is static locale text — the marker's error field is developer diagnostics (console marker only) and is never interpolated into the GUI; the read-and-clear semantics make the notice one-shot — the next boot sees null and stays silent; a record whose at timestamp is older than 48 h is suppressed and cleared with a console marker only — the timestamp bound is what closes the transition era, where the restored pre-feature binary's own prepare cannot remove the marker; a null outcome changes nothing on the boot path.

Renderer tests prove: a stubbed invoke returning the skip record shows exactly the localized sticky notice (once, key-formed title, the marker's error field absent from the GUI) even when the updater gate returns check:false (the gated-off boot case — e.g. autoCheckUpdates off via the facade stub); a null outcome shows nothing; a stale record (at older than 48 h) is suppressed and cleared — no notice, console marker only; the query failure path stays quiet (a boot notice must not be born from a broken fact channel — console marker only).

M-067's features.xml entry records the honest-async action contract, the truthful copy pulse and the action-failure notice; M-068's entry records the structured restore-outcome fact channel (marker + mt_rollback_restore_outcome) and the localized rollback-feedback surface; V-M-067/V-M-068 in verification/features.xml gain the new evidence (the exact test names this wave adds, in the living-tracker pattern); both amendments reference C-RENDER-REVIEW-FIXES; the edits land strictly after (or rebased on) C-STATS-READOUT's own deltas in the same two files — no entry of any other change is touched.

The LINKS headers of the seven governed source files (notificationCard, rollbackConfirm, editor.js, autoUpdates.js, services/notification, m068_rollback.rs, editorWithTabs/notifications.vue) gain .grace/changes/active/C-RENDER-REVIEW-FIXES alongside their existing references; the MODULE_MAP blocks of edited files are updated where the new locals/exports change them (the locale gate and the lint module-map checks stay green).

C-5.Expected: restore-outcome.json lives at rollback_root() itself (outside the consumed live/ set — it survives the restore's remove_dir_all and the boot finalization) and holds only {"prefs":"skipped","error":"<free-form diagnostics capped at 200 chars>","at":"<unix-seconds>"} — no dedicated path/digest/secret fields; written only at the shared macOS skip site, best-effort (a failed write never alters the restore outcome); stale copies removed at every restore entry and unconsumed copies at the prepare entry via the root-explicit removal helper (prepare_inner keeps its signature), with the at timestamp (48 h consumer window) bounding the fact across eras; mt_rollback_restore_outcome is read-and-clear — the read side enforcing the same bounds (an unparsable or over-long marker reads as null and clears) — and completes the four-site registration chain plus the app-store stub variant (the boot parity gate enforces the fixture↔allowlist pair in both directions; the hand-synced and transitively-covered sites are pinned by this plan's TargetAssertions); the restore algorithm itself is byte-unchanged beyond the additive channel.

C-6.Situation: Notification interaction latency and boot cost after the wave (awaits on action paths, one extra invoke on the boot path).
C-6.Expected: No synchronous blocking added (awaits are microtask-level; the pulse resolves within a frame of the write); the boot outcome query rides the existing awaited RUN_LAUNCH_CHECK path and a null answer costs one rejected-free invoke; no new timers or watchers.
